title: Dolma biber
subtitle: Stuffed peppers with spiced lamb and rice
excerpt: Dolma biber are whole green or red peppers stuffed with a spiced minced lamb and rice filling, then baked upright in a tomato sauce until the peppers are tender and the filling cooked through. Served warm as a main course with yoghurt.
sourceNotes: Claudia Roden, A Book of Middle Eastern Food (1968). Stuffed peppers documented across the Levant and Turkey as a summer dish when peppers are abundant. Aylin Oney Tan, A Taste of Sun and Fire (2014). Turkish biber dolmasi described as a family home dish.

recipe.freezeNotes: Cool completely, then freeze in portions. Reheat from frozen in a 180-degree oven for 25 minutes covered.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Stuff the peppers up to a day ahead, cover, and refrigerate. Bake straight from the fridge, adding ten minutes to the time.

content.text: Dolma biber are peppers stuffed with a mixture of minced lamb, uncooked rice, tomato, and warm spices, then set upright in a baking dish with a light tomato broth and baked until the peppers soften and the filling is cooked through. The rice absorbs the meat juices and the tomato sauce as it cooks. Serve with plain yoghurt.

items.prepNote: tops cut off and reserved, seeds removed

content.text: Preheat the oven to 190 degrees. In a bowl, combine {{lamb-mince}}, {{long-grain-rice}}, grated {{onion}}, chopped {{tomato}}, and {{tomato-puree}}. Add {{allspice}}, {{cinnamon-ground}}, {{sea-salt-fine}}, and {{parsley-flat}}. Mix well.

Fill each {{pepper-red}} and {{pepper-green}} to about two-thirds with the mixture (leave room for the rice to expand). Replace the pepper tops as lids. Stand the stuffed peppers upright in a deep baking dish.

Mix {{tinned-tomatoes}}, {{tomato-puree}}, {{sea-salt-fine}}, and 200 ml of water together. Pour this sauce around the base of the peppers in the dish. It should come about 2 cm up the sides of the peppers.

Cover the dish tightly with foil and bake for 45 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for a further 15 minutes until the tops of the peppers are slightly charred and the sauce is reduced. The rice inside should be fully cooked.
Rest for five minutes before serving. Serve with {{plain-yoghurt}} and the cooking sauce spooned around.

items.symptom: The rice is still raw after an hour
items.cause: Not enough liquid in the dish or foil not sealed tightly
items.fix: The foil must be tightly sealed to trap steam. If the sauce has dried out, add 100 ml of boiling water and re-cover.

items.symptom: The peppers have collapsed and are falling over
items.cause: They were not stood upright tightly enough
items.fix: Pack the peppers close together in the dish so they support each other. A dish just big enough for the peppers works best.

items.cause: Too much rice relative to lamb, or the dish ran dry
items.fix: Check the liquid level halfway through. The ratio of rice to lamb should be roughly one part rice to four parts lamb by weight.

items.symptom: The peppers are soft but the filling tastes flat
items.fix: Season the filling assertively before stuffing. Add a pinch of allspice to the serving yoghurt for extra depth.

content.text: Stuffed peppers are common throughout the eastern Mediterranean, Balkans, and Middle East. The Turkish biber dolmasi is typically made with the long, thin green peppers called carliston biber, which are sweeter and more tender than the blocky European bell peppers. Red bell peppers work well and are more available; a mix of colours makes the dish look festive. The filling is very similar to the stuffed courgette and cabbage roll versions: lamb, rice, tomato, allspice, and cinnamon are the regional flavour profile. In Lebanon and Syria, the dish is known as filfil mahshi and may include pine nuts in the filling.
